option_1.meaning: one leaf, seal and dogs rated for the full Delta-p from either side: a dog ring on the frame engaging the leaf's deck face besides the seat it already has on the tube side, a seal that is pressure-energized both ways, leaf structure checked for both load directions; the dogs retract before the 0.02 m drop and the 1.75 m slide
option_1.geometry: reverse dogs sit in the 0.05 m band between the leaf rim (r 0.85 m) and the guide rails (r 0.92 m) and must retract out of the leaf's slide path; the frame (0.22 m deep, skin to seat) carries them; no headroom or route change
option_1.mass_complexity: moderate: one more dog set and drive per hatch (x6); no new seal plane or pocket

option_2a_hinged_in_tube.result: FAIL: a 1.70 m leaf cannot stand edge-on in a 1.60 m bore

option_2b_tube_end_slide_gate.plate: r 0.85 m x 0.06 m at 24.43-24.49 m from the ring axis (seat on the inner hoop's inner face), travel 1.75 m
option_2b_tube_end_slide_gate.note: the tube ladder breaks for the closed plate; the plate carries the tube-side seal; same-rotor need = leaf swing clearance, swept need = mechanical clearance

option_2c_sector_side_plate.result: FAIL without lowering the ladder top and the landing light: the plate stack below the open leaf does not fit
option_2c_sector_side_plate.note: also puts the secondary inside the compartment it isolates (operated remotely only)

option_1.meaning: rate the tube hatch (or the drum door) for the full Delta-p from the vestibule side: dogs on its slide edges or a cam that clamps it to the face, a seal energized both ways; plate stiffness for the reverse load
option_1.geometry: inside the existing 0.04 m plate and 0.01 m track gap; the clamp/dog hardware sits in the track ends, outside the bore; no stack change measured
option_1.mass_complexity: moderate: x6 per ring, one of each pair

option_2a_door_on_inner_face.result: FAIL: the chamber holds the suited envelope between handrails with only 0.04 m spare, and the parked plate crosses the handrail between hatches

option_2b_hatch_in_running_gap.result: needs the ring face 0.05 m further out (tube root, collar and, on ring B, the neck base move); one plate then seats each way across the running gap

option_2c_collar_slide_gate.plate: r 0.85 m x 0.04 m at r 2.44 m in the 0.77 m radial collar, travel 1.75 m
option_2c_collar_slide_gate.note: a third closure per tube; seats from the vestibule side; needs a pocket enclosure on the collar

spine_gates.why: a vestibule or tube loss is then held by trunk pressure (the trunk serves the refuge, the other ring, docking, EVA and the storeroom); after a trunk loss the vestibule is reverse-loaded, but beyond it the drum doors and tube hatches seat from the tube side, so tubes and sectors stay pressure-held: the vestibule is an unoccupied transfer volume in that case
spine_gates.reverse_case: trunk loss with the vestibule at pressure
spine_gates.recommended_option: option 1 (bidirectional gate): option 2 does not fit the slot; a crew member in the drum during a trunk loss is the case that needs it

refuge.recommended_seat: from the refuge side (refuge pressure holds it when the trunk is lost: the haven case)
refuge.reverse_case: refuge breach while the trunk is at pressure
refuge.option_1: one bidirectional gate in the spine-shell slot (fits, see slot stack) or one hinged leaf with reverse dogs

option_2.primary: leaf hinged into the refuge, seats from the refuge side
option_2.secondary: slot gate seating from the trunk side
option_2.result: fits radially; the hoop and anchor rails beside the port are not checked against the swing (Blender)

R1 ring-local reserve (PREFERRED, spinni.where: on each rotor drum forward of its spoke plane, three segments between the crew tubes (ring A x [85.85, 87.05] m, ring B x [91.85, 93.05] m, r [1.62, 5.5] m)
R1 ring-local reserve (PREFERRED, spinni.protected_by: about 22.5 m radially from every sector, outside every pressure compartment, behind the remote fail-closed branch valve of each sector; a leaking sector or tube cannot reach it
R1 ring-local reserve (PREFERRED, spinni.path: reserve -> V-RES -> hub manifold -> V-BR-k -> line along crew tube k (in the tube wall chase) -> V-EQ-k at the tube-side hatch panel -> sector k; tube recovery via V-TB-k
R1 ring-local reserve (PREFERRED, spinni.source: S&E 16!A7 MEC-006: store/condition most fluids on the rotating side; bypass/isolation and local reserve

R4 stop and index (PREFERRED, recharge a.where: a recharge stab coupling beside the ring-stop lock housings (u -1.0 m, r 1.165 m outer pin), engaged only in STOPPED_LOCKED; stationary supply to the rotor manifold
R4 stop and index (PREFERRED, recharge a.path: stationary supply (source OPEN) -> stationary isolation + leak check -> stab coupling (engaged at index) -> V-RES fill valve -> reserve; backup: the same coupling feeds the hub manifold directly
R4 stop and index (PREFERRED, recharge a.limits: the ring's gravity is lost while stopped; the coupling geometry and mechanism belong with MEC-011 (OPEN)

R2 drum batch transfer (compared).path: pressurize the despun drum from the stationary side, synchronize, open drum door + tube hatch to the tube, repeat
R2 drum batch transfer (compared).limits: opens the transfer pair into the tube, so it cannot serve a leaking tube; each batch is bounded by the drum volume and the MEC-019 cycle (OPEN); the closures cycle under Delta-p; slower than R1, no hardware beyond the drum: kept as a tertiary path

R3 rotary gas union (NOT ADOPTED).why_not_needed: R1 covers the spinning emergency from rotating-side storage and R4 recharges at index, so no stationary-to-ring gas flow is needed while spinning; the hub keeps its one existing fluid coupling cartridge (Hub_FLUID_COUPLING, MEC-006) and adds no essential rotary gas interface (MEC-019)

rules: no gas into an actively leaking sector

crosses: sector hatch (closed; tube at 80 kPa, sector low: REVERSE-loaded)
rows.P1: BLOCKED until F1 has its rated reverse closure (option 1 dogs or option 2b gate) and it is tested: the repressurization itself holds the tube against the low sector on that hatch
rows.P2: interlock: V-EQ enables only after LC passes and the sector decay test shows the leak is stopped (threshold OPEN, Sheets); V-BR fail-closed
rows.P3: PASS: every valve on the tube side, at the hub or remote; no entry before the sector is at pressure

crosses: drum door + tube hatch (vestibule at pressure, tube low: REVERSE-loaded)
rows.P1: BLOCKED until F2 has one closure per pair rated or re-handed (option 1, or option 2b)
rows.P3: PASS: no strip is involved; the tube is entered only at pressure

rows.P1: PASS: no closure under reverse load
rows.P2: PASS: fills the reserve, never a sector directly

crosses: drum door + tube hatch (opened under equal pressure, cycled)
rows.P1: conditional: each cycle closes the pair with the drum at higher pressure than the tube unless equalized first (procedure, OPEN)
rows.P2: cannot serve a leaking tube; a sector only through V-EQ after LC
rows.P3: PASS: drum and tube are pressurized; never into a strip
